note: How a P7 answer is produced, and under what identity. The generator sees the question, its declared windows, and the retrieved reviews -- never the answer key, never the theme-shift direction, never a rating or a product's decline rank. `retrieval` is the retriever identity the evaluation run must match: changing any of it changes what every answer rests on, so it is hashed into the inference config alongside the prompt and the decoding schema.

retrieval.note: The production hybrid of ADR-0005, with the question's scope filter applied to both legs before fusion. Product-scoped questions retrieve ten over one window; temporal questions retrieve five per window, each window fused on its own, so an empty window cannot be filled from the other.

frozen_prompt.name: rag_v5

selected_on.set: development (ten questions, pre-2020 windows of non-candidate products)
selected_on.criterion: the citation and scope contract clean at 10/10, with the refusal branch reachable
selected_on.reason: rag-v1 and its successors were selected on contract behaviour alone -- no answer quality was scored, because scoring it would need answer keys and the only keyed set is the held-out thirty. rag-v2 fixed the citation vocabulary (contract 10/10, still 0 of 3 out-of-domain refusals). rag-v3 and rag-v4 added the subject test and the no-absence-as-a-claim rule in prose and moved 1 of 3. rag-v5 pairs the same prose with the decision-first schema and refused 3 of 3, plus two development products whose retrieved reviews are all praise, with the contract still clean at 10/10.

frozen_prompt.note: freeze_commit is the commit the development runs were made at; the commit recording this block is its child, so both are ancestors of the evaluation run.

amended.change: limits.subject_max_words (15) removed: it rejected two of the thirty evaluation answers unread, on a field nothing downstream consumes; the subject's length is now recorded per answer as subject_words. limits.max_attempts 2 -> 1: an identical retry of a temperature-0, seeded decoder returned identical token counts both times, so the retry is a no-op. Prompt rag-v5, model, seed and retrieval are untouched; the config hash moves because limits are hashed, and --reopen proves that is the only movement by recomputing the sealed hash with the sealed commit's limits.
